newsitem.title: USA: FBI narrows Olympic bombing time-frame.
newsitem.headline: FBI narrows Olympic bombing time-frame.

text.p: Investigators are closer to pinpointing the precise moment a deadly 40-pound (18-kg) pipe bomb was planted in Olympic Park last July, federal officials said on Sunday.

By painstakingly examining more than 4,600 still photographs and nearly 1,000 videotapes provided by the public, investigators have identified a 20-minute period when the backpack containing the device was left under a bench near the foot of a sound tower.
"We've actually narrowed it down to a time period of less than 20 minutes. But I can't be more specific than that," FBI spokesman Jay Spadafore said.

Authorities previously had been working with a 45-minute window, saying the bomb that killed two people and wounded more than 100 was planted between midnight and 12:45 a.m. (0545 GMT) on July 27 at a crowded concert in Atlanta's Centennial Olympic Park.
The device was discovered at 12:57 a.m. (0557 GMT) and detonated 23 minutes later, while police were still trying to clear the area of concert-goers at the height of the Atlanta Summer Games.

About 100 investigators assigned to the case are trying to identify and interview anyone in the park during the 20-minute period. U.S. Attorney Kent Alexander likened the task to setting up a video camera in a crowded shopping mall before Christmas and trying to identify everyone who walks past.
"One minute, you've got 150 faces in a frame. Thirty seconds later, you've got 150 new faces. That's the kind of scene you're dealing with," he told the Atlanta Journal-Constitution.
Investigators have not determined if there are links between the Olympic bombing and the double-bomb attack that injured six people at an Atlanta abortion clinic on Jan. 16.
"There's no evidence that the two bombings are linked," Spadafore said, but he acknowledged that investigators had not been able to rule out a link.
